newsitem.title: UK: Russian Urals crude skids in Med, perkier in NWE.
newsitem.headline: Russian Urals crude skids in Med, perkier in NWE.

text.p: Spot market values for distillate-rich Urals crude in the Mediterranean, usually riding high at this time of year as refiners rush to produce heating oil ahead of winter, was on the skids on Wednesday, traders said.

Three or four large cargoes of the Russian grade due to load in the first 10 days of November were on offer against thin demand from refiners wallowing in sweet Nigerian barrels bought earlier this month.
"Urals margins are quite good at current numbers, but that's no use if you haven't got any room in your tank," said one.
A very prompt million-barrel Urals cargo traded at Dated Brent -$1.11 a barrel, c&f Med, on Tuesday, more than 30 cents cheaper than a sale last Friday.
A second cargo of a similar size was also heard sold into a Black Sea port, but details could not be confirmed.
"The first decade (of November) is looking a bit clearer but there are still three cargoes available. I'm looking for a bid," said a trader.

Traders valued Urals at about Dated Brent -$1.15 a barrel, cif Med, on Wednesday but said it could slip further. "If I were a buyer I would be bidding about 20 cents below yesterday's level," said one.
"It looks as if the wait-and-see approach adopted by some refiners has been productive," said another.
A tightening of European diesel emission specifications on October 1 was forcing some refiners with inadequate desulphurisation capacity to increase their intake of sweeter grades.

With the flow of Nigerian barrels to the U.S. squeezed in recent weeks by an unfavourable Brent-WTI spread, those refiners had taken the opportunity to fill their tanks when Urals was relatively expensive, traders added.
Other Med grades were looking pricey after the Urals losses and traders said a Syrian Light sale at a small premium to November's OSP of Dated Brent -5 cents would not be repeated.
The prospect of surplus Urals moving from the Med to northwest Europe, where prices were edging higher, was the only glimmer of hope for sellers.
A U.S. major was considering taking a large cargo into its own refining system in NWE after it attracted little spot market interest.
In NWE, Petroleos de Venezuela SA (PDVSA) subsidiary Lagoven bought two 500,000-barrel Urals cargoes for late November delivery for its refining operations in Germany.
Traders said the cargoes were sold for about Dated Brent -80/85 cents a barrel but pegged the spot market value closer to -65 cents.
